hero.title: The project behind the store
hero.subtitle: Cyber is not a startup and not a template from a marketplace. It is a hand-built e-commerce platform written to prove that the whole stack — from database schema to checkout flow — can be done properly.

what.title: What is {store}?
what.p1: Honest answer: {store} is a personal project and a portfolio piece. Every feature here exists because it was designed, implemented, debugged and shipped by one developer — not copied from a tutorial.
what.p2: The store is fully functional: products with variants, real cart and order lifecycle, reviews with reactions, coupons, admin panel with roles and audit trail. It runs on the same code path in demo and in production.
what.fact1: Personal portfolio project, built from scratch
what.fact2: Full commerce loop: catalog → cart → checkout → orders
what.fact3: Admin panel with roles, moderation and settings audit log

stack.title: Tech stack
stack.subtitle: The tools actually used in production, each doing a job it is good at.

nextjs.name: Next.js 15
nextjs.desc: App Router with [locale] segment, server components for catalog and admin surfaces, streaming with Suspense boundaries.

typescript.name: TypeScript
typescript.desc: Typed where it matters — shared logic, validation and tests — while UI keeps the speed of plain JSX modules.

database.name: PostgreSQL + Prisma
database.desc: Real relational schema: products, variants, stock, carts, orders, coupons, reviews — with foreign keys and cascade rules.

auth.name: NextAuth
auth.desc: JWT sessions with roles (user / admin / super_admin), credential and OAuth providers, server-side guards on every route.

i18n.name: next-intl
i18n.desc: English, Russian and Persian translations for the whole UI, including RTL layout support for Persian.

styling.name: Tailwind CSS
styling.desc: Design tokens as theme variables, four switchable themes, component classes shared across the app.

media.name: S3 media
media.desc: Product and avatar images uploaded to S3-compatible storage, normalized to public CDN URLs.

hosting.name: Vercel
hosting.desc: Continuous deployment from the main branch, preview builds for every pull request.

devops.name: Docker
devops.desc: Local PostgreSQL in a container, reproducible dev environment for the database and migrations.

arch.title: Architecture notes
arch.subtitle: The project follows Feature-Sliced Design: entities, features, widgets and pages, each slice owning its own model and UI.

fsd.title: FSD layers
fsd.desc: Cross-imports only downward: pages compose widgets and features, features use entities, shared code lives in the shared layer.

actions.title: Server-first data
actions.desc: Prices, discounts and totals are always recalculated on the server; the client never decides how much an order costs.

admin.title: Guarded admin
admin.desc: Role checks run on the server for every admin page and action, and settings changes are written to an audit log with author and before/after values.

features.title: What works here
features.subtitle: Real features of the running store — no mockups, no screenshots of other people's code.

catalog.title: Catalog with variants
catalog.desc: Categories, product variants by color/storage/RAM, specs, search and related products.

reviews.title: Reviews & reactions
reviews.desc: One review per product per user, star rating, likes and dislikes, reporting and admin moderation.

wishlist.title: Wishlist
wishlist.desc: Per-user saved products with instant sync from product cards and the header counter.

coupons.title: Coupons
coupons.desc: Percentage and fixed-amount coupons with validity windows, usage limits and one-time rules.

orders.title: Orders
orders.desc: Sandbox checkout creating real orders: line items, totals, status lifecycle, returns and cancellation.

wallet.title: Admin settings
wallet.desc: Store name, contacts and commerce rules editable in the admin panel, versioned in the audit log.

dev.name: Maivand Rahmani
dev.bio: Designed and built {store} alone — schema, server logic, UI and deployment. The source is public: read it, run it, judge the work by the code.
